newsitem.title: FRANCE: France declines comment on Iran spy charge.
newsitem.headline: France declines comment on Iran spy charge.

text.p: French authorities declined to comment on Wednesday about a possible connection between Iran's secret service and an Iranian student expelled from France.
"There is no comment," a French Foreign Ministry spokesman told reporters who brought up the issue.
The Iranian National Council of Resistance, an Iraqi-backed armed opposition movement, had said in a statement from its Paris office that the expelled man was an Iranian intelligence agent.
It said that under cover of preparing a doctorate in engineering, he was passing scientific intelligence to Iran and contacting Islamic fundamentalists in France.

The French spokesman confirmed a report by the official Iranian news agency IRNA that Iran's Foreign Ministry had summoned the French charge d'affaires in Tehran to protest against the expulsion of "an Iranian student studying in France under scholarship".
The protest came at a time of frayed relations between Iran and France and its European partners.

The European Union pursued a policy of "critical dialogue" with Iran until all EU states but Greece withdrew their ambassadors from Tehran in April following a German court ruling that Tehran leaders ordered political killings in Germany in 1992. Iran denied the accusations.
